title: Universal property of G ×^P X' and induction by stages
body_html:
Universal property of $G \times^P X'$ and induction by stages

Universal property

Let $Y$ be a $G$-space, and define $$\mathrm{Map}_{G',P}(X', Y) := \{f : X' \to Y \;|\; f \text{ is } G'\text{-equivariant and } P_x \subseteq \Fix_G(f(x)) \text{ for all } x\}.$$

Proposition. The assignment $f \longmapsto \widetilde f$ with $\widetilde f([g,x]) = g \cdot f(x)$ is a natural bijection $$\mathrm{Map}_{G',P}(X', Y) \;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\; \mathrm{Map}_G(X, Y).$$
proof_html:
Well-definedness of $\widetilde f$ uses $(g,x) \sim (h,y) \Rightarrow y = nx$ and $g^{-1}hn \in P_x \subseteq \Fix_G(f(x))$, hence $h \cdot f(y) = h n \cdot f(x) = g \cdot (g^{-1}hn) \cdot f(x) = g \cdot f(x)$. Conversely, for $\Phi \in \mathrm{Map}_G(X,Y)$, set $f(x) := \Phi([1,x])$; $G'$-equivariance follows because $\Phi$ is $G$-equivariant, and the $P_x$-fixing condition follows from $[1,x] = [p,x]$ for $p \in P_x$.

Induction by stages

Let $G'' \le G' \le G$, and suppose $P$ is a cosheaf of subgroups of $G$ on a $G''$-space $X''$ satisfying (P1)–(P2) for $G'' \le G$. Set $P'_x := P_x \cap G'$ (a cosheaf for $G'$) and $X' := G' \times^{P'} X''$, and extend $P$ to $X'$ by $\widetilde P_{g' E} := g' P_E (g')^{-1}$.

Proposition (induction by stages). There is a canonical $G$-equivariant bijection $$\Phi \colon G \times^{\widetilde P} (G' \times^{P'} X'') \;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\; G \times^P X'', > \qquad \Phi([g, [g', x]]) = [g g', x].$$

Proof. Verify that the LHS satisfies the same universal property as the RHS. For $f \in \mathrm{Map}_{G'', P}(X'', Y)$, define $\widetilde f([g',x]) := g' f(x) \in \mathrm{Map}_{G', P'}(G' \times^{P'} X'', Y)$, then extend to $\widetilde{\widetilde f} \in \mathrm{Map}_G(G \times^{\widetilde P}(G' \times^{P'} X''), Y)$. The map $f \mapsto \widetilde{\widetilde f}$ is a natural bijection. $\square$

This stages identity is exactly what extends the generalized-building cosheaf $K$ from the apartment $A$ to the full Bruhat–Tits building of $G'$; see Generalized building B(Σ) = G ×^K A.
